analysis.investment_thesis: Graphite India is perhaps the most dangerous-looking stock in this batch: an 8% ROE, a 2.80% operating margin, negative EBITDA in FY24, OCF negative in 3 of 5 years, and an EV/EBITDA of 63x — the reported P/E of 38.2x is entirely a function of massive 'other income' (1,258 Cr in FY24, 438 Cr in FY25) that dwarfs the actual operating business. This is a cyclical commodity business disguised as a profitable one by one-time income.
key_strengths: Near-debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.05) and 5,884 Cr equity base provide financial resilience through prolonged downturns
Global leadership in graphite electrode manufacturing with specialized products across a range of industrial applications
Forward P/E of 15.06x implies the market expects earnings normalization — if the electrode super-cycle returns, upside could be significant
key_risks: Operating business is currently loss-making at EBITDA level (FY24: -46 Cr EBITDA) — the reported profits are driven by extraordinary other income, not operations
Revenue has contracted from a 7,858 Cr peak in FY19 to 2,560 Cr in FY25, and operating margins at 2.80% provide no buffer against any further deterioration
Graphite electrode prices are set by global EAF steel demand and Chinese competition — Graphite India has demonstrated zero pricing power through the post-2019 downcycle
red_flags: EV/EBITDA of 63x is extreme — this is a valuation that assumes either an imminent commodity super-cycle or a permanent improvement in earnings that operating data does not support
FY24 'other income' of 1,258 Cr (versus operating income of -143 Cr) inflated all per-share metrics and likely triggered retail interest in a fundamentally weak business
OCF negative in FY22 and FY23, positive only due to investment income — a manufacturing company whose operations cannot consistently generate cash is deeply problematic
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Graphite India's FY19 experience — when electrode prices spiked due to a Chinese supply shock and the company earned 5,020 Cr in operating income on 7,858 Cr revenue — was a once-in-a-decade windfall, not a business model. The years since have revealed the true economics: thin margins, no pricing power, and operating losses in bad years. The current 2.80% operating margin and 8% ROE are the real Graphite India, not the FY19 outlier. A business that earns its cost of capital only in supercycle conditions is not one I wish to own.

The FY24 reported profit of 805 Cr was built on 1,258 Cr of 'other income' while the core business generated negative EBITDA. At 38.2x P/E on these distorted earnings — and 63x EV/EBITDA on actual operating earnings — the stock prices in a supercycle recovery I am not qualified to predict. I never buy a commodity business at peak-cycle prices, and I certainly won't buy one at these multiples when the cycle is clearly depressed.
